The colors of the mountains and the moon represent the four seasons: green for spring, blue for summer, orange for autumn, and purple-blue for winter. You can try your luck to see which color you get!  

This work is my final project for a blockchain application course. It combines the noise-generated mountains taught by Professor Huang Xin, a moon and stars made of dots, and a gradient night sky. Along the way, I incorporated modifications to the code suggested by ChatGPT. Ultimately, I completed my first blockchain-based creation, which also serves as a reflection of my learning achievements this semester.

Bomb or Shine, which one do you like?

And if it is a bright light, even if it shines hard, it may still be swallowed by darkness.

But even so, spikes and lights can be useful. When facing people with malicious intentions, use spikes to protect yourself; when facing weak and helpless people, use lights to illuminate the way forward. Become a person who embraces the world with gentleness without losing your sharpness!

*This is an extension of a NewYellow's class exercise where I tried to produce a variety of variations*

Each piece begins as a blank canvas, where invisible currents of Perlin noise guide particles through space, leaving traces of their journey like dancers writing their choreography in light.
The artwork unfolds uniquely each time, with particles manifesting as flowing lines, sharp angles, or ethereal circles, each guided by unseen mathematical forces. Some compositions peak early and freeze in their prime, while others develop slowly, building complex layers before reaching their final form. Colors range from cool celestial hues to warm earthen tones, with occasional bursts of light punctuating the composition like stars in a dynamic cosmos.

Cosmic Currents: Digital Dreamscapes
In the vast expanse of digital space, where mathematics meets imagination, a realm exists where particle flows transcend their algorithmic origins. Each iteration tells a unique tale of convergence - sometimes spiraling in harmonious patterns like celestial bodies in orbital dance, other times breaking into chaos like cosmic storms across nebular fields. The work draws inspiration from both the microscopic flow of quantum particles and the macroscopic dance of galactic formations.
This generative piece explores the delicate balance between order and chaos, structure and fluidity. Through its four distinct composition types - centered, asymmetric, grid, and radial - it mirrors the fundamental patterns found throughout nature, from the sacred geometry of crystalline structures to the organic flow of ocean currents. Each viewing reveals a new configuration, a unique moment frozen in digital time, where colors and forms collaborate to create unrepeatable moments of digital synchronicity. The varying densities and movement patterns echo the natural world's tendency to create both moments of intense activity and peaceful voids, all working in harmony to create a singular artistic expression.

The 人人 collection aims to achieve the simplest possible expression using 3D objects. 人人 is a Japanese word. The pronunciation is "hitobito," and it means "people."

Quantum Veil: A Symphony of Algorithmic Art
A work of algorithmic art interwoven with the mathematical harmony of the chaotic universe. Quantum Veil transcends the limits of modern software to transform ever-changing forms into a captivating visual symphony. Through precise mathematical models, this piece introduces order within randomness, immersing the viewer in a mesmerizing exploration of chaos.

Inspired by the quantum vibrations of nature and the infinite expanse of the cosmos, each frame captures the fusion of scientific discovery and artistic expression.

Dynamic Movement: Constantly evolving fluctuations offer a unique visual experience in every moment. These movements, generated by mathematical wave functions, symbolize the vibrational energy at the core of existence.
Color and Light: A balanced palette of soft tones and inverted contrasts invites the viewer to explore the universe's dynamic nature. Pressing the 'r' key shifts the scene from the purity of white to the infinity of black, embodying the ever-transforming cosmos. Pressing 's' allows you to capture a .png snapshot—a reflection of the ephemeral and infinite nature of digital art.

Attention Quantum Veil Owners
This artwork is a labor of love, crafted by an emerging developer. While every effort has been made to refine it and enhance its artistic elements, its experimental origins remain a key part of its charm.

You may encounter similar color tones during minting due to their closeness. This phenomenon aligns with a mathematical probability:
Probability = (1 / 16,777,216) × 100 ≈ 0.00000596%.
This calculation includes subtle hues that the human eye cannot easily distinguish.
Your understanding is greatly appreciated, and I hope this work of art offers you a truly unique experience.

Interaction Instructions
Press 'r': Transition between the purity of white and the infinity of black.
Press 's': Save a unique .png snapshot of your moment.
Dimensions: 400 x 400 px

我很愛看海，對我來說，它是可以讓我心靈平靜、靈感泉湧、包容我一切的存在。所以基於這個理由，我想讓大家都能擁有屬於自己獨一無二的海，希望你們在看這片海的時候也能因此獲得一些啟發。

這片海是由很多層浪組建而成，每個人的海浪層數和顏色都不太一樣（但仍然保持在一定範圍之間），這象徵沒有人的經歷能被別人取代；而天象則有三種，分別是太陽、月亮和星空。我將太陽營造出夸父追日、線條拖曳之感，月亮則是溫柔地散發光暈，星星則像活力滿滿的孩子在跳動一樣；海底的泡泡則是可以互動的，當滑鼠靠近，泡泡就會羞澀地躲開，你可以跟「她」玩捉迷藏。

以上是關於作品的一些背景跟內容介紹，希望所有鑄造作品的人都能喜歡這片深沉卻又不失斑斕的海洋。

I love watching the sea. For me, it is a place that can calm my mind, inspire me, and embrace everything about me. So for this reason, I want everyone to have their own unique sea, and I hope you can get some inspiration when looking at this sea.

This sea is made up of many layers of waves. The number and color of each person's waves are different (but still within a certain range), which symbolizes that no one's experience can be replaced by others; and the celestial phenomena are There are three types: the sun, the moon and the starry sky. I made the sun look like Kuafu chasing the sun, with lines dragging, the moon emits a gentle halo, and the stars jump like energetic children; the bubbles on the seabed are interactive, and when the mouse approaches , Bubble will shyly hide away, and you can play hide-and-seek with "her".

The above is some background and content introduction about the work. I hope that all those who created thｉｓ　ＮＦＴ will like this deep yet colorful ocean.

How do you see the world?

How sure are you about your truths?

31548.d:
In physics, the theory of everything strives to fully explain and link together all aspects of the universe. The closest, physicists have come so far to this theory, is quantum mechanics.

The quantum realm is most obscure and intriguing. I am fascinated about it since I studied basic physics. 

Looking even deeper inside the building blocks that make up atoms, everything becomes unimaginable. Quantum behaviour, hyperspace and parallel dimensions are only explainable in mathematical formulas. The strange behaviour can be observed in experiments E.g.

- Spooky action at a distance Two separate Particles a kilometre apart from each other behave synchronised. 
- The double slit experiment A beam of electrons behaves as a stream of separate particles -like trickling sand- as soon as you measure it. If you don’t try to measure it, it behaves like an expanding wave -like on the surface of water-. 
- Schrödinger’s cat experiment An imagined cat in a box is dead and alive at the same time
- Quantum tunnelling A particle can cross barriers they should not be able to
- Brane Theory An multidimensional object inside a quantum can at the same time be as large as the whole universe or even bigger.

All things we call reality are made up by frequencies, oscillating waves and membranes. Everything is connected through these waves, frequencies, energy.

I love these frequencies because they produce patterns that emerge in nature on all different scales. From electrons circling around a nucleus to planets circling around a star.
From bubbles in foam to possible multiverses in dimensions our minds cannot grasp. There is always pattern and structure in what seems random and chaotic.


My fxhash project T.O.E. is an abstract artistic vision of the quantum realm. It is inspired by pattern that emerge in the architecture of atoms; the inner arrangement of solid matter, like e.g. crystallisation; by images generated in particle collisions; by visualisations of string and brane theories and by the energy I can feel everywhere around me.

Disclaimer: The math behind this project is not based on real physic formulas

31549.d:
She has a boyfriend who loves her deeply, yet she secretly drifts among various men. By becoming the third party in others' relationships, she fulfills her desire to be someone’s special preference, finding a sense of so-called uniqueness. 

However, these relationships bring her both joy and sorrow. She revels in the thrill of forbidden love and the feeling of being someone’s favorite, yet she suffers from the instability, lack of future, and emotional turmoil inherent in such connections. 

Through my work, I aim to portray the protagonist’s enigmatic inner world, using shifts in color to reflect the contrasting emotions she experiences as a devoted girlfriend and as someone else’s third party, showcasing the different states of mind she navigates within these complex relationships.

她有很愛她的男友，卻在背地裡遊走在各式各樣的男人間；透過成為他人之間的第三者，從中滿足她想成為對誰而言的偏愛、進而獲取所謂的特殊感。但這樣的關係卻也讓她快樂與痛苦並存著，享受著偷情、成為偏愛的快樂，卻也對這樣不正常、沒有未來、充滿不安全感、患得患失的關係感到痛苦。我想透過作品呈現出主角撲朔迷離的內心，並透過顏色的變化來呈現她作為一個女友、他人的第三者之間，在不同的關係中所展現的不同的心境。

"Digital Confluence" is an exploration of the intersection between mathematical precision and organic chaos. Each piece emerges from a complex interplay of flow fields, geometric patterns, and mathematical noise, mirroring the natural phenomena found in both cosmic and microscopic scales. Like the flowing patterns of turbulent fluids or the intricate formations of crystal growth, the artwork generates unique compositions that balance order and randomness. The color palettes - ranging from deep urban nights to vibrant neon dreams - represent different emotional and temporal states, while the varying densities of lines and shapes create a sense of depth that draws viewers into contemplating the underlying patterns that connect all forms of natural and artificial complexity.
The multiple generation modes in the artwork symbolize different states of consciousness and perception. The flowing fields represent the continuous stream of thoughts and energy, while the geometric patterns echo the underlying mathematical principles that govern our universe. The grid patterns suggest human attempts to organize and understand chaos, and when these modes combine in the "mixed" state, they create a visual metaphor for the beautiful complexity that emerges when different systems of order and chaos interact with each other.

31573.d:
From Classic Inspiration to Modern Exploration: Dragon Curve Vortex

My latest generative artwork, Dragon Curve Vortex, draws inspiration from a foundational text in the field of computer art: Computer Graphics/Computer Art by Herbert W. Franke. On page 4, I encountered the dragon curve, a mathematical fractal that sparked Franke's series of plotter drawings titled DRAKULA (translated as "Dragon Curves, Superimposed"). These works, produced in collaboration with computer scientist Josef Vordermaier, utilized a program Vordermaier created to generate the imagery.

For many years, I carried the influence of this 1970s concept. Just as Franke had Vordermaier, I have my collaborator, Christopher Scussel. Together, we embrace the spirit of revisiting old ideas through a contemporary lens. In this vein, I challenged Chris to craft a new, interactive fractal algorithm for me to explore programmatically.

A Fractal Dance

A dragon curve is a self-similar fractal curve, constructed using recursive methods like Lindenmayer systems. In Dragon Curve Vortex, this mathematical form transforms into a dynamic spatial entity. I generate a vortex by selecting a random number of curves, each with a varying level of complexity, to spin at diverse angles around the image center. To introduce a touch of visual intrigue, the artwork incorporates a distortion field. This field, a canvas of bulges and dents, stretches and compresses the vortex while maintaining the integrity of the underlying fractal pattern. Color selection is also driven by controlled randomness, adding another layer of captivating dynamism.

Interactive Exploration

The essence of generative art lies in its ability to evolve and surprise. Dragon Curve Vortex embodies this concept by allowing you, the viewer, to actively participate in its creation. Simply press any key to refresh the display and witness a new iteration of the artwork emerge.

A Celebration of Collaboration

Dragon Curve Vortex marks a significant milestone – my 101st generative art piece published on fxhash. This achievement is a testament to the power of collaboration and the enduring allure of artistic exploration.

I invite you to join me in celebrating this journey and delve into the mesmerizing world of Dragon Curve Vortex.

Please visit www.drbillkolomyjec.com

31591.d:
Code Point Assembly is a procedurally generated NFT that transforms Unicode characters into a mesmerizing, mirrored landscape, radiating symmetrically from a central point. Each palette is dynamically composed using a single color, which is then shifted to the 16 standard terminal colors to create a stunning visual gradient.

This generative art piece offers both PNG and animated PNG outputs, allowing collectors to experience its evolving, algorithmic beauty in motion.

Interactive Controls:
🔹 H - Set DPMM (Dots Per Millimeter) to 3.2 (high detail)
🔹 L - Set DPMM to 0.8 (low detail)
🔹 K - Set DPMM to 1.6 (medium detail)
🔹 C - Set startup color to a random selection to get palette variations of your piece
🔹 A - Toggle animation of an expanding vignette
🔹 S - Download the generated image

Each iteration of Code Point Assembly is a unique visual experience, an interplay of code, typography, color, and chaos—ready to be minted, collected, and admired in its infinite variations.

Built with a Go powered WASM engine using:
- gdamore/tcell
- tdewolff/canvas
- kettek/apng
- digitallyserviced/{palettic,unispider}

Organic Chaos is a generative artwork that captures the beauty of structured randomness. Each piece is created through an evolving process where thousands of particles follow unique curved paths, resulting in a mesmerizing, fluid composition.

Every artwork is generated from a single initial seed, but the user can interact and reshape the piece, adding new layers of complexity with each action. The chaotic yet harmonious distribution of strokes, combined with controlled symmetry, gives each iteration a unique character.

How It Works
🖱 Mouse: Click to add new trails to the artwork.
🔄 Spacebar: Regenerates the entire piece with the same initial seed, maintaining a consistent visual identity.
Key "1": Draws only the left half and mirrors it for perfect symmetry.
Key "2": Draws only the right half and mirrors it for an alternate symmetrical balance.
🎭 Key "0": Removes symmetry, allowing a fully organic distribution of strokes.
💾 Key "S": Saves the current artwork as an image file, preserving the unique moment of creation.


Every mint is a one-of-a-kind generative composition, evolving through interaction, randomness, and symmetry. Whether chaotic or balanced, each piece is an exploration of movement and organic structure—an artwork that exists between order and entropy.

"Fractured Blossoms" is a digital generative artwork that explores the tension between organic growth and chaotic fragmentation. The intricate network of branching structures, interwoven with toroidal forms, evokes a biomechanical ecosystem—an alien garden where nature and abstraction collide. The piece reflects the fractured state of our contemporary world, where beauty and disorder coexist, mirroring both environmental and geopolitical crises.

Technically, the piece is created using procedural growth algorithms generating plant-like structures that evolve dynamically in a digital habitat. The use of MatCap materials enhances the interplay of colors and reflections, giving the composition an almost metallic, fluid-like quality. This hybrid aesthetic, blending biological references with synthetic textures, invites the viewer to question the boundaries between the natural and the artificial, the organic and the technological.

Stripes, often regarded as a "pure form," serve as symbols of national flags, identity, power, and control. In the realm of digital media, they are also closely linked to programmatic approaches. When painted by hand, the inherent distortions and irregularities introduce noise, highlighting the materiality of the medium.

This work is a piece of generative art that explores the contrast between order and fluidity within stripes. The number of stripes, their colors, and the way they appear to drip are randomly determined, creating a unique composition each time.

The colors are selected randomly from five different palettes, each consisting of twelve colors. These palettes ensure a sense of harmony while allowing for a wide range of variations. As a result, the artwork remains both fresh and cohesive in its color composition.

Additionally, the dripping forms of some stripes evoke the flow of paint and the passage of time, incorporating a dynamic element into an otherwise static pattern. This interplay of system and chance, order and deviation, reflects the dynamic possibilities inherent in digital art.

The objects move around randomly. They travel while rotating within a certain range at random speeds. When they collide with another object, they stop, rest for a while, and then start moving again. The movement rules are simple and mechanical, yet at the same time, they somehow appear organic.

This piece is a 3D work created using Three.js. You can control the camera by clicking the mouse or tapping the screen. Additionally, double-clicking the screen changes the speed at which the objects move. The speed changes from 1x -> 2x -> 4x -> Stop, and then returns to 1x.

The 人人 collection aims to achieve the simplest possible expression using 3D objects. 人人 is a Japanese word. The pronunciation is "hitobito," and it means "people."

This evolutionary progression transforms an initially simple order into complex and mesmerizing patterns over time. Just like in nature, every small interaction is part of a grand transformation. The universe of cellular automata is a dynamic structure that follows rules yet remains full of surprises.  

This collection was created to explore the aesthetic and mathematical beauty of cellular automata. Each piece visualizes how a complex order emerges from simple rules. The interactions between colors, forms, and structures reveal the depth and power of the system's rules. Inspired by iconic collections such as "RGB Elementary Cellular Automaton," my goal with this project is to bring together the evolutionary beauty of fundamental rules in both natural and artificial systems and to open a window into the essence of these models through an interactive approach.

This generative artwork employs computational algorithms to create visually dynamic and intricate designs based on two primary adjustable parameters: symmetry and central shape. These parameters guide the structure and appearance of the design, with each interaction resulting in a unique output.

Symmetry and Radial Patterns: The artwork is based on a radial symmetry principle, meaning the design is mirrored across multiple segments arranged around a central point. The number of segments is controlled by the symmetry parameter, which divides the circle into equal parts. This approach ensures that the design remains balanced and evenly distributed. Each segment mirrors the others, creating harmonious patterns that radiate outward.

Central Shape Variation: The central portion of the artwork features one of several geometric shapes, which can range from simple polygons to more complex forms like stars or concentric ellipses. The shape's appearance is determined by the central shape parameter, adding variety to the overall composition. The use of different geometric shapes serves to anchor the design and provides a focal point in the center of the artwork.

Layered Structure: The design is built up through multiple layers, each of which varies in size and structure. These layers are concentric circles, with each successive layer having a smaller or larger radius. The edges of each circle are slightly distorted using randomness, creating organic, wavy shapes. This randomness introduces natural variation into the design, preventing it from appearing too rigid or mechanical.

Color Palette: The colors in the artwork are generated dynamically using a system based on the HSB (Hue, Saturation, Brightness) color model. A base color is chosen, and the hues shift slightly for each layer, ensuring a smooth transition between colors. The saturation and brightness are also varied to add visual depth and complexity, creating a rich, multi-dimensional effect.

Particle Effects: Small, random particles are scattered throughout the design, adding texture and detail. These particles are placed in a way that complements the symmetry of the overall design, enhancing its dynamic and organic feel.

Petal-like Elements: Around the central shape, petal-like structures are drawn, adding complexity and movement to the design. These petals are created through organic curves and random variations in size and shape, contributing to the flowing, dynamic nature of the artwork.

Interactivity: The artwork is interactive, allowing users to adjust the symmetry and central shape parameters. This interactivity ensures that each viewer can create a completely unique version of the design, providing a personalized experience. As the parameters change, the artwork is dynamically updated, generating new, one-of-a-kind patterns with each adjustment.

In summary, this generative artwork combines principles of symmetry, randomness, and color theory to create visually appealing and diverse designs. By integrating user input with algorithmic processes, the artwork explores how computational methods can be used to produce unique, evolving visual compositions that engage both the viewer’s sense of aesthetics and curiosity.

The code creates a generative artwork based on random elements, blending various shapes, colors, and particle effects. The central theme revolves around symmetry, sacred geometry, and dynamic particle systems. The artwork is rendered on a canvas, and the visual composition evolves based on randomly generated parameters that influence shapes, colors, and movement.

Key Concepts and Techniques Used
Canvas Setup:

The canvas is set to a square resolution (1080x1080 pixels) and uses the HSB (Hue, Saturation, Brightness) color mode to easily manipulate colors. Angles are measured in degrees.
Randomized Parameters:

Several parameters are randomized to introduce variability in the artwork. These parameters include:
Symmetry: Controls how many symmetrical copies of a shape are drawn (e.g., circles or lines).
Angle: Defines the angle between each symmetrical copy.
Layers: Refers to how many concentric layers of geometry are drawn, with each layer having a smaller radius than the previous one.
Colors: Color palettes are randomly generated for both the doodle elements and the sacred geometry. This allows the artwork to change with each execution.
Doodle Elements:

Various types of doodles (blobs, spikes, scribbles, etc.) are created and randomly placed on the canvas. Each doodle element has random properties such as size, rotation, color, and complexity.
These elements are designed using procedural techniques, where their shapes evolve based on mathematical functions (e.g., noise or randomness).
Sacred Geometry:

Sacred geometry patterns are generated at the center of the canvas. These patterns are made up of concentric circles and lines, creating complex, symmetrical designs that are repeated multiple times, based on the symmetry value.
The geometry is drawn with a focus on repetition and rotational symmetry, resulting in a kaleidoscope-like effect.
Particles:

A particle system is used to generate dynamic visual elements like confetti, sparkles, and trails. Each particle has random properties, such as its size, color, movement speed, and life span. These particles move and change over time, adding a sense of motion and liveliness to the artwork.
When particles move off-screen or reach the end of their lifespan, they are reset to a new random position to keep the system active.
Background Effects:

A gradient background is created to enhance the visual experience. The gradient is applied across the entire canvas, transitioning from one color to another. This subtle effect sets the tone for the artwork and adds depth.
Final Touches:

The artwork ends with a vignette effect, which darkens the edges of the canvas and draws focus toward the center. This softens the overall composition and adds a more polished, finished look.
Visual and Aesthetic Features
Symmetry and Geometry: The artwork has a harmonious structure, with shapes and patterns following a symmetrical layout. Sacred geometry is a key component, with rotating circles and interconnected lines forming intricate designs.

Dynamic Elements: Doodle elements (blobs, spikes, scribbles, etc.) bring organic and chaotic forms to the artwork. These elements are randomly generated but maintain an overall cohesive style through their color and shape types.

Particle Interactions: The particles add life to the artwork, moving around and interacting with the environment. Their varied behaviors (confetti, sparkles, trails) make the piece feel alive and ever-changing.

Color Palettes: The colors used in the artwork vary between vibrant, complementary hues and more muted tones, depending on the randomization of color palettes. This keeps the visual experience fresh with every rendering.

Polished Look: The vignette effect and the harmonious placement of doodles and geometry create a balanced composition that is visually pleasing and focused on the center.

31641.d:
Generative Artwork Exploring Particle Dynamics & Flow Fields

Concept & Inspiration
"Viscous Flux" visualizes the tension between controlled systems and chaotic fluid dynamics, inspired by the behavior of high-viscosity fluids navigating constrained environments. The work draws parallels between industrial piping systems (represented by maze-like walls) and organic flow patterns, using computational physics to simulate particle interactions. The ever-changing flow field echoes natural phenomena like magnetic field lines or weather patterns, while the algorithmic color system nods to oxidized metal patinas.

Key Technical Components

1.
Particle Engine
2,000-6,000 particles (user-configurable) with mass-velocity relationships
HSL color space interpolation based on velocity vectors
Viscosity simulation via velocity damping factor (μ = 0.287)
Collision detection with maze walls using AABB (axis-aligned bounding box)
2.
Dynamic Flow Field
Perlin noise-driven vector field (20px resolution grid)
Triple noise offset (xOff, yOff, zOff) for temporal evolution
Force application using p5.Vector normalization and magnitude mapping
3.
Maze Architecture
Parametric wall generation with quadrant gap algorithm
Four primary walls containing 25%/75% entry points
Signed-distance field calculation for obstacle avoidance
4.
Physics Model
Newtonian mechanics implementation: F = m * a
Velocity clamping at user-defined maximum (1-5 units/frame)
Boundary condition handling with velocity inversion
Parameters & Features
Controlled through FXHash parametric system:

Parameter	Range	Effect
Base Size	3-9px	Particle diameter seed value
Max Velocity	1-5	Speed ceiling for turbulence control
Base Hue	0-360	Core color theme (HSL space)
Particles	2000-6000	System complexity/density
Wall Hue	0-360	Maze color (vs particle contrast)
Features include real-time particle count tracking, obstacle complexity analysis, and emergent size distribution patterns.

Interaction Dynamics

1.
Flow Field acts as perpetual force generator (toggle with 'F')
2.
Mouse Input creates radial attraction/repulsion forces
3.
Boundary Collisions maintain energy within the system
4.
Noise Z-Offset creates gradual field metamorphosis over time
Particles exhibit:

Velocity-dependent opacity (50-255 alpha)
Mass-correlated acceleration response
Hue drift constrained to ±30° from base value
Technical Execution
Built with:

p5.js for rendering pipeline
FXHash wrapper for parameterization
HSL color space for perceptual uniformity
Monte Carlo methods for initial particle placement
Frame rate stabilized at 30 FPS through:

Spatial partitioning for collision checks
Pre-computed obstacle geometry
Lookup tables for trigonometric operations
Artistic Intent
This work questions the dichotomy between engineered systems and organic motion. By implementing real fluid viscosity values (0.287 Pa·s matching 15W-40 motor oil), it grounds digital abstraction in physical reality. The constrained maze becomes a metaphor for algorithmic boundaries in generative art, while particles represent creative possibilities navigating these structures.

The piece achieves its signature aesthetic through controlled randomness - Perlin noise drives both particle motion and color variation, creating emergent patterns that feel simultaneously intentional and naturally evolved.

Production Notes
To render: Execute in FXHash environment with WebGL acceleration. Final output captures frame 1500 (50s runtime) to show developed flow patterns while maintaining particle density. Cold hues suggest industrial fluids; warm tones evoke lava flow dynamics.

"The Golden Hour," is my generative art project that attempts to blur the lines between generative art and photography. Inspired by the magical moments of twilight, dusk and dawn.

The Golden Hour is a fleeting yet magical window just after sunrise and just before sunset, offering a palette of warm, soft light that transforms the ordinary into the extraordinary. This project aims to evoke that same sense of wonder.

On a small screen or mobile device, I want viewers to question whether they are looking at a photograph of a landscape. Upon closer inspection, it becomes clear that these are generative artworks, not photographs. Of course, with the number of mints available, I have had to introduce more randomness, so I know that some will not necessarily give that impression if they have a bright magenta sky. This element of unpredictability ensures that every piece is distinct, offering a fresh perspective on the interplay between code, art and nature.

------------------------------------------------
Press s to save the image.
Press e for endless animation.
Press p to pause animation.
------------------------------------------------

To save at a higher resolution, open the live view of your token, add &scale=3 or &scale=4 to the end of the URL. Be mindful that larger outputs will take longer to render. The default scale is 2.

I used the p5js JavaScript library to create this collection and minify-js to minimise the files.

Jean-Paul Sartre suggested that relationships often involve objectifying others to fulfill our own sense of meaning.

Early humans survived in tightly knit tribes where recognizing and remembering individuals (even from stories) had value. This instinct to form attachments, even to those we don’t interact with directly, persists today. From mythological heroes to religious figures, humans have long admired and emotionally invested in distant, often idealized personalities.

Parasocial relationships are neither inherently good nor bad. They provide comfort, motivation, and even emotional stability for some. They can inspire creativity, self-improvement, or community formation. However, they can also distort perceptions of reality, encourage consumerist manipulation, and lead to emotional dependency.

The key question is balance. As Plato warned about being ruled by illusions, one must distinguish between meaningful social bonds and fabricated intimacy. Codescape is my generative art project that explores the harmony between urban landscapes and digital creation. Inspired by the quiet moments of looking out my window — where the city’s silhouette meets a sky painted with sunsets, drifting clouds, and flickering window lights — this project captures that fleeting balance between simplicity and beauty.

Each render presents a unique skyline, shaped by procedural randomness to reflect the ever-changing nature of city views. One moment, it’s a serene sunrise casting warm hues over the rooftops; the next, a deep, starry night with glowing windows resembling distant constellations.

My goal is to evoke the feeling of gazing at a real cityscape while subtly revealing the hand of code beneath it. At first glance, it might feel like a stylized photograph or a painted skyline — but upon closer inspection, the abstract geometry, evolving clouds, and layered randomness expose its generative heart. This unpredictability ensures no two skylines are ever the same, offering a dynamic, digital reimagination of the urban horizon.

31671.d:
A lone knight embarks upon an uncertain quest,
Dancing between order and chaos, leaping with restless intent.
Each step, a decision—each turn, a twist of fate—
Until a path is carved, glowing with the colors of time.

"Crazy Knight Line" is a generative artwork created in p5.js, inspired by the unconventional movements of a chess knight. Unlike a predictable linear path, this piece constructs an evolving, jagged trajectory based on random step sizes (s1, s2). The knight moves across a dynamically defined grid, creating a unique journey for each execution.

Key elements of the algorithm:

The grid size (cols, rows) is randomly chosen, ensuring variety in each render.

The knight's movement is based on L-shaped jumps, constrained by the grid's boundaries.

The number of steps is randomized, making each drawing distinct in complexity.

The movement path is drawn as a sequence of connected lines, smoothly transitioning between colors from cyan (start) to deep blue (end) using lerpColor().

This interplay between structured rules and randomness generates a striking, unpredictable composition—chaotic yet mesmerizing, evoking the wandering mind of a knight lost in an infinite game.

石庭や苔寺がこの作品のインスピレーションの始まりでした。
お寺や神社を散歩するうちに、公園の樹木の樹皮や苔などにも自然と意識が向くようになりました。

スケッチをするように、リアルで写実的な表現をp5.jsで目指しましたが、
技術的に伴わなず、壁にぶつかることも度々ありました。

それを補うように、苔や水、草木や花のような表現を思いつくままに
岩の上を覆うように重ねて遊んでいました。

最初はより自然的な絵に仕上げようとしてましたが、
次第にデジタルで機械的な表現をおり混ぜたいとも思い、
自然なノイズの中に、整列された機械的な要素が見え隠れするような、
対比のある表現を目指していました。

初期段階では想定してなかった思いつき、コードと向き合う中で日々通り過ぎていくような遊びを
色々なパラメータとして振り分けていきました。

４つのモードに分類しています。

・レイアウト
・四季
・描画モード
・その他パラメータ

特別なレアリティなどは設けていませんが、
たくさんのバリエーションを楽しんでいただけたら嬉しいです。



Zen rock gardens and moss temples were the initial inspiration for this piece.
As I wandered through temples and shrines, I began to naturally notice the textures of tree bark and moss in nearby parks as well.

Like sketching in a notebook, I aimed to recreate realistic, detailed expressions using p5.js,
but I often ran into technical limitations and obstacles.

To fill in those gaps, I began layering expressions of moss, water, plants, and flowers on the rocks,
freely experimenting and playing as I went.

At first, I intended to create something that felt more natural and organic.
But gradually, I also wanted to incorporate digital, mechanical elements—
to create a contrast where orderly, artificial forms subtly emerge within natural noise.

Unplanned ideas—fleeting moments of play that came to me while coding—
were gradually transformed into various parameters.

The piece is structured around four modes:
	•	Layout
	•	Seasons
	•	Drawing Modes
	•	Other Parameters

There are no special rarities or exclusives,
but I hope you enjoy exploring the many possible variations.

31683.d:
A generative artwork built with p5.js and custom GLSL shaders that simulates the aesthetic of a 56 kbps dial-up experience in a retro Internet Explorer interface. The piece renders as a progressively loading image, a digital nod to the sluggish pace of early network connections. At first, the image materialises in fragmented scanlines and intermittent glitches, capturing the nostalgic feel of old Windows 98 UIs.

Interactivity lies at the heart of the work: while the progressive loading offers a dynamic view of the creation process, you can press the "F" key at any moment to toggle to a full-resolution rendering. This allows you to appreciate both the process and the finished, detailed image that emerges once the simulated loading is complete.

Each mint is unique, with subtle variations from randomised loading artefacts and connection drop simulations woven into the code. Ms. Paint_56kbps is a playful yet precise exploration of digital-era limitations transformed into a new visual language.

31688.d:
Broken Unknot is an abstract textural geometric exploration of an initial state of idealized perfection that has fallen from grace into an imperfect state.  The artist contends that the imperfect form is preferable to the perfect form - embracing flaws and inconsistencies, eschewing rigor and formality.

Each composition begins with a single unbroken circle (topologically an "unknot") that is coiled in various manners to fill the page space.  It is then decorated in a manner analogous to stringing beads onto a necklace, including the possibility for unexpected variations in the sequencing of the bead pattern.  That perfect circle and its decorations are then subjected to various abuses.. including breaking the chain into multiple disconnected segments, potentially eliminating loose beads in the process, quantizing it onto a regular lattice, and virtually shaking it into various deformations.

Released as two separate versions for BASE and TEZOS that are loosely synchronized to produce iterations that are of similar "character".  That is, while each version will differ in the specifics of generation, the more-general parameters affecting more-major aspects of the composition will be similar for any given iteration number between the two versions - in a diptych-like manner of semi-matching pairs.  Clever minters might be able to intuit a rough idea of potential future output from one version based on prior minted iterations of the other version.

This work was designed for producing plot-ready vector output for a physical pen plotter.  The on-screen (raster) image is only intended to simulate how a physical plot might appear.  As such, the on-screen rendering is intentionally minimalistic, with few other distractions from the raw pen traces.  Upon close inspection, the detailed plotter paths are intentionally revealed in the preview - no solid fills are used, despite any illusion of such that might occur at small scales.

CONTROLS:

Press 'p' to save PNG at current resolution
Press 's' to save SVG (current resolution doesn't matter)

Press a number key to adjust resolution (prior to saving PNG):
'1' : 1100px x 1700px (11" x 17" @ 100dpi)
'2' : 2200px x 3400px (11" x 17" @ 200dpi)
'3' : 3300px x 5100px (11" x 17" @ 300dpi) (default)
'4' : 4400px x 6800px (11" x 17" @ 400dpi)
'5' : 5500px x 8500px (11" x 17" @ 500dpi)
'6' : 6600px x 10200px (11" x 17" @ 600dpi)

DIY plotting tips:  First, there are no rules, so feel free to use whatever combination of pens, paper and color you wish.  Having said that, if you wish to mimic the screen output, even if just as a starting point for further exploration:  At native scale, a nib diameter of about 0.4mm on 11" x 17" smooth paper is suggested.  Will also fit at native scale centered on A3 paper, though the margins will vary.  If scaled up/down to fit larger/smaller paper, adjust pen size accordingly.  Finer pens will tend to reveal the spiral fill pattern and create a more open feel, while broader pens will tend to merge adjacent forms and create a denser feel.  Expensive implements are not required - even a "cheap" ballpoint pen, on "cheap" office paper, can produce pleasing results.  Generally it is best to plot lighter colors first, followed by darker colors - so if using custom colors you may wish to alter the plot sequence to accommodate.  You may plot multiple layers with the same color to reduce the total number of colors, or even elect to not plot certain layers at all to increase white-space in the composition.  You might also try varying the pen size on colors you wish to emphasize/deemphasize.

Note that this generator is capable of producing occasional dense outliers that may be more challenging to plot successfully.  A summary of the resulting plot complexity is provided in the console after generation - for planning purposes, if needed.

Discover the mesmerizing world of "Celestial Harmony," a generative art collection where ancient symbolism meets modern digital creativity. This series, crafted for fxhash, invites art collectors to explore the profound beauty of mandalas through intricate, algorithmically generated designs that evoke balance, unity, and spiritual depth.

What is a Mandala?
The mandala, derived from the ancient Sanskrit word for "circle," is a sacred symbol found across cultures, from Tibetan Buddhism to Native American traditions. It represents the universe, wholeness, and the journey toward inner harmony. Traditionally, mandalas are symmetrical, geometric patterns that radiate from a central point, often used in meditation to focus the mind and connect with the divine. Their hypnotic designs draw the viewer inward, offering a sense of peace and contemplation.

In this collection, each mandala is a unique, algorithmically generated masterpiece, blending traditional symmetry with contemporary aesthetics. The artworks feature:
•	Dynamic Layers and Patterns: Multiple layers of petals, waves, spirals, and radial forms create a sense of depth and motion, drawing the eye toward the center.
•	Harmonious Color Palettes: Choose from six distinct styles, ranging from soft pastels (blues, pinks, mint greens) to vibrant triadic hues (red, green, blue) and bold complementary tones (purple and yellow). Each palette is carefully curated to evoke emotional resonance—whether calming, energizing, or grounding.
•	Central Flower Motif: At the heart of each mandala blooms a delicate flower, symbolizing growth and renewal, surrounded by intricate, symmetrical patterns that radiate outward like cosmic energy.
•	Subtle Variations: Small, intentional imperfections in symmetry and curvature add an organic, handcrafted feel, making each piece feel alive and unique.

31694.d:
We’ve always known wallet addresses as strings of letters and numbers—dry, soulless data, yet always present.  
We decided to transform this constant presence into a living image.  
Instead of remaining mere tools for transactions, these addresses are turned into unique, enduring works of art—digital fingerprints that forever belong to their owners. A signature that always stays with its creator.

In a world where everything began with pixels—from the first games to the earliest digital artworks—we chose to reimagine your digital identity through pixels, intertwining the spirit of pixel art with the structure of the wallet itself.  
As a result, each pixel creature born in this project is generated directly from the structure of the wallet address (fxminter) and the artwork's hash (fxhash).

Each creature in this project is a synthesis of these two unique data points.  
Colors, forms, and even the sequence in which the creature appears are entirely derived from them.  
The piece begins with an intelligent system analyzing your identity.  
Then, these data are translated into pixel creatures, built in three distinct sections, emerging with colors extracted from the hash.  
No two creatures are alike—each is a living, one-of-a-kind reflection of its holder.

But this is only the beginning...

Holders of tokens from this project (Season One) will unlock a hidden layer within their artwork—one that is not visible at first glance.  
It’s as if an abstract image, a subconscious imprint, rests quietly behind the pixels.  
A layer that will only be revealed with entry into Season Two.

This piece marks the first season of a long-term project—one crafted with a multi-season perspective.  
With each season, not only do the meaning and form of the artworks evolve, but the value of the tokens increases over time—not just in visual terms, but as fragments of a living narrative, where each season uncovers a new layer of *you*.

Only the holders of Season One tokens will possess the key to enter Season Two.

The work sits at the intersection of atmospheric abstraction and symbolic representation,
where generative aesthetics become a vehicle for an exploration of the perceptual threshold between form and dissolution.
Vertical structures, resembling slender shrubs or nervous filaments, construct a visual lattice that oscillates between transparency and density, suggesting a synthetic vegetation suspended between nature and algorithm.

The composition stands out for its use of digital color, with gradients that simulate traditional techniques such as pastel or watercolor, while maintaining a coherence typical of code. The generative intervention is not merely ornamental: it is a formal strategy that translates the indeterminacy of the landscape into an autonomous aesthetic language.

The sinuous shapes that emerge from below and rise upwards are not mere presences: they suggest a humanity in the making—or rather, an anthropomorphic echo generated by the system, a tension between organic mark-making and computational logic.

Nesting is a generative art project that creates dynamic grid-based compositions inspired by Windows 98's visual aesthetic.

The project features recursive nested grids with the following key characteristics:
- Creates grids of varying sizes (1x1 up to 6x6)
- Uses Windows 98-style borders (outset/inset) and colors
- Implements recursive nesting of cells with adjustable probability
- Allows cells to merge into larger units (2x1, 1x2, or 2x2)

Features four main customizable parameters:
- Grid Size: Controls the main grid dimensions (1-6)
- Cell Border Style: Determines border appearance (outset/inset/mixed)
- Nesting Probability: Controls how likely cells are to contain nested grids (0-0.8)
- Merge Probability: Affects how often cells combine into larger units (0-0.5)

The result is a dynamic composition that combines the rigid structure of a grid system with organic variations through nesting and merging, all styled with a distinctive retro Windows 98 aesthetic.

Harmonic Eccentricity is a generative meditation on chaos and symmetry, built through layered revolutions of motion and hue. Radiating from a central stillness, geometric forms — lines, arcs, triangles, rectangles, and bezier curves — spiral into an orchestrated rhythm of color and balance. Each form is born from randomness, yet bound by circular order, echoing both organic growth and digital precision.

Created entirely with p5.js, this piece leverages the power of code to compose a symphony of dark tonal depth, where each stroke emerges from a unique chromatic logic governed by hue-shifting mathematics. With a dark, moody backdrop and rich, low-saturation colors, the result evokes ancient mandalas filtered through a modern algorithmic lens.

The structure is static, frozen in the moment it was algorithmically conceived — each render a one-of-a-kind iteration drawn by a unique seed, never to be repeated.

Harmonix transforms algorithmic logic into immersive, colourful, architectural forms. Each render constructs a digital landscape from extruded blocks of gradients, arranged within a grid, producing a visual rhythm that feels both mechanical and musical—hence the name. 

Rather than depict static geometry, Harmonix thrives on contrast and iteration. It explores how a simple set of generative rules can give rise to wildly different environments - chaotic cities of stacked signals, minimalist code-scapes, or layered harmonic grids. 
The result is a modular symphony of form and colour.

31722.d:
The kanji (Japanese term for Han Chinese characters) for love—as a general concept—is 愛, which is romanized as "ai" and pronounced like "eye". Hence, PR愛DE. I know it's a couple of weeks away, but some say every month is Pride Month, and every minute of every day those of us who experience identity, love, and desire in ways most folk find strange deserve to feel real, and seen, and free to be who we are—so I'm minting 5/8, which is kinda auspicious. I also tried to apply plenty of auspicious number instances for good luck. Of course I hope this artwork brings you luck and joy, and that you stay safe and hopeful out in the world (or not *out* in it, whatever is best for you).

I tried to make sure everyone has some representation by using colors from the Progress Pride Flag, and I made the background grey because we’ve all been there, in a grey area on the way to understanding our true selves—and some of us find that we are defined by being in a grey area, or by being people for whom the options for feeling romantic or intimate desires are “greyed out”.  And for those of us whose lives are drab grey because we cannot safely live authentically, that’s for you, too; I see you.  PR愛DE is for all of you—all of *us*—even though there will only be 835 of this particular design.  This is far from being the only Pride NFT I’ll create.  (And feel free to use the basic design to make your own version with the colors you want—for your own personal enjoyment, of course.)

Be well, y'all.
31722.c: Each edition is an image 3600 pixels square, nice 'n big for printing and displaying on a wall or wherever you like.  The backdrop is always grey, and the other eleven color regions each receive at determinist random one of the eleven unique colors of the Progress Pride Flag.  Each of the eleven colors appears exactly once.  Note: this is a static image, and only the placement of the colors differs from edition to edition.

31729.d: This is the Monochrome version of Taijitwo Twist, all black and white from the outermost arcs on in.  I based this pair of NFTs on the imagery presented on the Wikipedia article for “Taijitu”.  These designs incorporate an old design of Taijitu, with concentric arcs, and at the center a modern design many people think of when Yin and Yang are mentioned, with the interlocking shapes similar to the Japanese tomoe and magatama.  Two taijitu, hence Taijitwo.  The arcs of the old design, however, are not uniformly arranged about a central axis and the thicknesses don’t match from side to side.  It ends up resembling a circular maze to a varying degree, which, I suppose, can represent the paths we end up taking in life.  Sometimes we feel shifted towards Yin or towards Yang, some periods in our lives are darker and some are lighter.  While the effort of striving for balance is commendable, Taoism teaches that the point of perfection in life (analogous to Buddhism’s nirvana) is by living in a state of Wu Wei, acting by not acting—letting the Tao guide one’s behavior, as opposed to one’s desires or society’s expectations.  So, one might say that if we allow the Tao to show us the path through the maze, we will eventually come to the bliss of the Taiji’s perfect balance.  One might also say that the semicircle-stacking method I used is a metaphor for ascending towards a higher state of being.  Take all this with a grain of salt; I’m still learning about the Tao, and still quite a novice.  For y’all, I’ve included “$fx.minter” so that any of this collection you purchase will have design(s) determined in part by your wallet address, in tandem with the hash.
31729.c: I used p5.js for this work.  The design is generated by three random sequences: one for the angles from one pair of arcs (each half of a circle) to the next, and these arcs are formed by overlaying progressively smaller filled arcs—black and white semicircles.  The other two sequences determines the thicknesses of the apparent arcs, with each arc in a pair using a different sequence.  So far as the pushed matrix is rotating from one pair of arcs to the next, the arcs on each side of the matrix independent of the rotation use the same sequence, i.e. the left uses one sequence and the right uses the other.  Also, the apparent left and right arcs change color from pair to pair, so that each pair has one black and one white.  The Modern Taijitu at the center involves opposite-color rings against the halves to increase their definition in the image, and the symbol itself is a layering of same-radius filled arcs and circles.

I wanted to reflect on the concept of error, imperfection, and change. In a historical moment where everything must be beautiful, perfect, and aligned with an idealized aesthetic, approaching what is ugly, embracing complexity, imperfection, and turning mistakes into the spark of transformation, feels, to me, like an act of inner liberation.

This project aims to highlight the importance of the unexpected. It reminds us that mistakes can lead to growth. Change breaks monotony, shatters predetermined order, acts as an agent of chaos. It reshapes and improves what we see and what we feel.

This glitch is based on a grid composition. The image is built from a series of squares placed in sequence, and characterized by a gradual chromatic control. To stimulate movement and fluidity, I added different compositions that randomly break the linearity of the pattern. This generates "jumps" and "fractures", bringing rhythm and energy to the final composition. The result is a hypnotic pixel dance—part textile, part broken screen, or simply whatever it evokes for you.

Just like in everyday life, something can always come along to disrupt our plans. Embrace the unexpected. Live life to the fullest.

The grid gives structure for marking change, but the work isn’t about precision. It’s about rhythm, growing, filling up, and breaking free.

The SENTINELS, with their cold, diamond forms, reign over an unsettling realm. Their presence exudes an aura of solemn guardianship, shrouded with unease. These are not friendly guides; they are silent arbiters of the unknown, both protectors and judges of the enigma that is their terrain. As you gaze into their world, let these haunting apparitions remind you of the vastness of the cosmos. 

The SENTINELS beckon you to explore the sinister beauty of the abyss, to question, and to wander through a digital realm where the eerie and the captivating coexist.

Paranoia is a necessary skill whenever a SENTINEL is involved.
 
SENTINELS is not only an exploration of the sublime-it also empowers collectors to generate physical artifacts from the void. With a keystroke, you choose your format:

Press ‘s’ or ‘1’ to save a compact version
‘2’ for a print-ready image
‘3’ for a high-resolution image

31745.d:
"A Cidade Que Inventamos" is a pattern created with the Clojure Patterning library in 2022 at an artistic residency in Buinho Rural FabLab in Messejana, Alentejo in Portugal.

The pattern constructs a random city-scape from a number of tiles, some of which have their own internal variations. One of the quirks of the Patterning library is that grids are, by default, filled column-wise rather than row-wise. This naturally leads to creating a stylised city from vertical runs of tiles, leading to tall, narrow buildings that are somewhat inspired by the clock-tower and chimneys of Messejana.

Many uses of the pattern are intended to be static. I've laser-engraved it on wood tiles, game boards, and on "blank" panels for modular synthesisers. However, for this version on FX(hash) some slight dynamic variation has been introduced. The clocks show the current time. And the position and density of the people varies slightly with the time of day. 

Multiple versions of this pattern can themselves be tiled together to make a yet larger city. The original exhibition featured a larger laser-engraved panel made of 5 x 4 smaller city-scape tiles.

31747.d:
We’ve always known wallet addresses as strings of letters and numbers, Dry, soulless data, yet always present.
But what if this presence could breathe?

In the enhanced, living version of "Season One", we revisit that same idea, transforming the blockchain’s most essential elements into evolving pixelated lifeforms.
Each artwork is still generated from the wallet address (`fxminter`) and the token’s hash (`fxhash`), but the project pulses with a new kind of energy this time.

### What’s new in this evolved version:

🕰 A Magical Clock
A real-time clock has been embedded into the artwork. One that only ticks forward with each new mint.
Each minted token captures a unique minute in time, held eternally by its collector.
This enchanted clock is not merely decorative. It holds a secret that will only be fully unveiled in "Season Two".

🧩 A Fragment of the Bigger Picture
Alongside the creature, every mint now receives a Roman numeral representing its mint number and a coordinate, marking its position in a hidden puzzle.
Each token is a piece of a larger design; together, these fragments will reconstruct the gateway to the next season.

🧬 Multiple Perspectives, One Identity
The core pixel creature, still generated uniquely from your wallet and hash, now appears in three views:

* a breathing 2D form rendered in real time,
* a puzzled isometric shape,
* and a miniature preview of the final Season Two puzzle form, hinting at what’s to come.
  Your identity is no longer shown from a single angle, it’s a multidimensional expression.

🎨 Colors from the Hash, Signatures from the Wallet
Like in the original version, all color palettes are derived directly from the hash. No two are alike.
And, as always, your wallet address is subtly signed beneath the artwork, a permanent mark of authorship.

---

This is not Season Two.
This is Season One: Alive, an evolved, living version of the original.
It preserves everything that made the first release special, but adds movement, time, spatial positioning, and hints of the next chapter.

If Season One was a spark, this version is its flame.
Only holders of these tokens will be able to step fully into Season Two and witness the transformation of their piece into its final narrative form.
Until then, this is your moment. Your pixel, your minute, your breath in the story.
